source.description:
PROBLEM: service-knowledge (~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge, v0.1.0, Python pkg: cli/canary/contracts/dispatch/eval/index/mcp/install/skills) is not agent-first: agents must grep for service-registry.json, drift handling is repo-local folklore (mercury-infra PoC only), and agents have no doctrine for what to do when knowledge is stale. Verified assets: existing wrapper extension core/packages/pi-extensions/extensions/service-skills/index.ts (134 lines: resolveRegistryPath umbrella/flat precedence, cataloger.py wiring); drift marker mechanism in mercury/infra (.xtrm/.service-skills-drift-pending: "drift detected post-merge on main; services: 14; files: 53; action: run /updating-service-skills + stamp last_sync_ref"); pi extension scoping (docs/extensions.md: global vs project-local .pi/extensions, project_trust lifecycle).

DESgist PRINCIPLES: (1) self-gating beats per-repo install: extension ships globally in @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions but registers ZERO surface when no registry exists in cwd - the "check then use, not before" becomes invisible, no trust ceremony, no wasted context. (2) never block on knowledge updates: stale registry is used as-is; update is suggested + queued; work proceeds; commits are the fallback memory (git log -p --follow, corpus). (3) drift check -> suggest -> reconcile -> stamp last_sync_ref -> rebuild index, all non-blocking. (4) python synergy: service_knowledge is importable in-kernel once skillbridge (core xtrm-h7uwi.1) lands - drift check + index rebuild as function calls, same gating signal (registry presence) can drive a per-repo driver prelude.

CHILDREN: ext self-gating v1; drift loop generalization; commit-corpus doctrine + system-prompt landing (prompt block done in-session); kernel binding (depends core xtrm-h7uwi.1).

NON_GOALS: no MCP server changes; no per-repo extension installation requirement; no blocking gates on drift.
